chunks: From him, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara ibn A'yan, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'What do you say regarding sleeping in the mosques?' He said, 'There is no harm in it, except in the two mosques: the Mosque of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and the Sacred Mosque.'

He said, 'And he used to take my hand in some part of the night, so he would sit in a corner, then sit down and converse in the Sacred Mosque. So sometimes he slept, and I slept. So I spoke to him regarding that, so he said, 'It is only disliked to sleep in the Sacred Mosque which was in the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). But as for sleeping in this place, there is no harm in it.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sleep in the mosques according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the general permissibility of sleeping in mosques and the specific reverence due to the two holiest sanctuaries, noting that the prohibition primarily applied to the original structure of the Sacred Mosque during the Prophet's era. This hadith highlights the Shia scholarly nuance in distinguishing between the physical location and its historical sanctity, allowing for practical accommodation in the current expanded structures while maintaining respect for the Prophet's Mosque and the Kaaba's immediate precincts. It underscores the principle that sleeping in mosques is not inherently impeding unless it disrespects the specific sanctity of these key sites.

en.hubeali: From him, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara Bin Ayn who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding the sleeping in the Masjids. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem with it except in two Masjids – The Masjid of the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>, and the Sacred Masjid’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And he<sup>asws</sup> used to grab me by my hand in one of the nights, so he<sup>asws</sup> ended up in a corner. Then he<sup>asws</sup> would sit down and narrate in the Sacred Masjid. So sometimes he<sup>asws</sup> slept, and I slept (as well). So I spoke to him<sup>asws</sup> regarding that, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But rather, it is disliked if one were to sleep in the Sacred Masjid which was upon the era of Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>. But, as for the sleeping in this place, so there is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 11. It is a narration from him (narrator of previous Hadith) by his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, Alayhi al-Salam, about sleeping in Masjid. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not an offense, except two Masjids: Masjid of the Holy prophet and Masjid al-Haram.’

He (the narrator) has said that he (the Imam) would in certain parts of the night hold my hand and move to one side where he would sit and speak in Masjid al-Haram and perhaps sleep and I also sleep. I then spoke to him about it and he (the Imam) said that it is undesirable to sleep in Masjid al-Haram that was in the time of the Messenger of Allah but sleeping in this area is not an offense.’”
